content:
alex: Heads-up — since ~02:10 UTC we've been seeing short bursts of local-disk IO saturation in eu-south1 during the nightly ephemeral-cleaner window. GPU attach times jump and several batch jobs time out while waiting for scratch volumes.

jamie: saw that too. spikes line up with the janitor run that reclaims old scratch files. attach latencies from 120ms -> 2.3s for a few minutes.

nina: any corruption reports or just latency?

alex: no corruption alerts; it's pure throughput/IOPS exhaustion. cloud metrics show per-host NVMe saturation + queue depth rise. logs: ```
2026-03-19T02:11:03Z cleaner[pid=2384] delete: /scratch/tmp/abc123
2026-03-19T02:11:04Z kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1048576
2026-03-19T02:11:05Z gpu-provisioner: attach start -> delay, retrying
```

liam: blk_update_request line worries me but correlation not causation. could be heavy fsyncs from the cleaner (stat+unlink patterns) + our scrub threads hitting same underlying blocks.

jamie: quick repro: run the cleaner on a gnode with heavy scratch churn and you get queue_depth > 128 and many requests at ms > 50. GPU attach times out after 30s in the worst case.

nina: current mitigations? can we throttle the cleaner or move it off-peak?

alex: I bumped cleaner concurrency to 2 in the eu-south1 schedule and that helped for the next window; attach latency dropped but still had small blips. we should consider a few options: 1) rate-limit janitor deletes per-host, 2) use staggered windows per-AZ, 3) pre-warm scratch volumes (allocate smaller quota pools), 4) fallback GPU routing to eu-west if attach > X ms.

liam: prefer 1 + 2 asap. Staggering windows is low-risk. Also suggest adding a quick circuit-breaker in the attach path: if local NVMe avg iops > threshold, route to spare capacity.

ops-bot: incident-note created: INCIDENT-20260319-012 - eu-south1 ephemeral-cleaner IO surge affecting gpu attach. Pager schedule: eng-oncall.

jamie: cost tradeoffs: routing to other regions increases cross-region egress/cost and latency for users. but so does job retrying while waiting for attach. need numbers.

nina: on dedicated capacity customers we should avoid cross-region fallback by default. maybe honor "dedicated:true" by skipping routing and instead queue job/notify.

alex: agree. short-term plan: (A) push a config to limit cleaner concurrency to 2 per-host for next 3 windows, (B) roll staggered windows across AZs starting tonight, (C) instrument attach path to emit NVMe queue_depth + iops metrics and add routing threshold.

liam: long-term: look into making cleaner unlink pattern more batching-friendly (bulk unlink + deferred fsync) and investigate moving heavy metadata ops onto separate ephemeral partitions where possible. also consider proactively scrubbing less aggressively on high-wear devices to reduce write amplification.

jamie: I'll own the rate-limit + stagger rollout. alex can you add the attach metrics + circuit-breaker PR? nina, can you draft the customer-safe fallback policy for Dedicated vs Hosted?

nina: on it. will propose policy doc and a short FAQ for support.

alex: creating PR now for attach-metrics and an emergency toggle. linking here when ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: update: INCIDENT-20260319-012 acknowledged by eng-oncall.

liam: after the first reduced-run we saw attach latencies drop ~65% and no timeouts. keep monitoring and we'll reconvene after the next window.

jamie: will follow up with cost estimate for regional fallback vs job queuing.

alex: thanks all. if anyone sees corruption or persistent read errors please escalate immediately and add logs.

nina: noted. will sync with support on customer comms if needed. :phone:

(End of thread)
